title: 1. The Hook: The Mystery of the Old House
text: Imagine travelling in a time machine to 70 years ago. Your great-grandparents are building a new house, but there is no cement, no iron rods, and no big cranes! How did they build strong houses without these modern things?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Nature's Building Blocks
text: If you had to build a house today using only things you could find in a forest or a village field, what would you use for the walls and the roof? Why do you think people long ago mixed cow dung with mud to coat their floors? What would happen if they only used dry sand?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Evolution of Houses
content.description: Watch how a house transforms from a simple mud hut with a thatched roof to a strong brick house, and finally to a modern apartment building.

title: 4. The Reveal: Changing Materials
text: Over time, the materials we use for building houses have completely changed. Early houses were made of unbaked bricks, mud, wood, and straw. To keep insects away, floors were coated with mud and cow dung. Later, people started using baked bricks, which are much stronger. Today, we use cement, sand, iron rods (lintel), and concrete to build very tall and strong buildings.

content.definition: A horizontal beam made of iron or wood placed across the top of a door or window to support the wall above it.
Bricks made from mud and dried in the sun, but not baked in a hot oven (kiln). They are less strong than baked bricks.

content.text: Encourage students to think about why different regions use different materials (e.g., bamboo in earthquake-prone areas, sloping roofs where it snows). Context is key!

content.mistake: Thinking that mud houses are always weak and break easily.
content.correction: Mud houses are very eco-friendly and keep the inside cool during hot summers. With proper maintenance, they can last for many generations!

content.question: Why did people in earlier times coat the floors and walls of their houses with a mixture of mud and cow dung?
options: To make the house look beautiful and colorful
To keep insects and bugs away from the house
To make the house smell like a farm
To dry the floor faster after raining

content.question: Which of the following materials is used in modern houses to make the roof extremely strong?

title: 6. Reflection: Your Own Home
text: Think about your own house or apartment. What materials is it made of? Look at the walls, the floor, and the ceiling. Explain in your own words how your home is different from a house built 100 years ago.

title: 7. Connection: The Web of Change
text: Changing times don't just affect houses! Just like building materials improved from mud to cement, our vehicles upgraded from bullock carts to fast cars, and our communication changed from writing letters to using smartphones. Technology and discovery connect everything in our lives.

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Grandparent Interview
content.text: Be a history detective! Talk to your parents or grandparents. Ask them to describe the house they grew up in. What was the roof made of? Where did they cook food? Draw a picture of their old house and compare it with the house you live in today.
